requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 169/169 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The new README section and the MsgPack004 doc state that diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly. This is consistent with the deliberate behavior in [L8], so it is not a defect. The ledger records that metadata types are not analysed by the consuming project.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The README claims closed generic types from referenced assemblies get no diagnostics from the consumer. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter drops every diagnostic whose location is outside the compilation. Closed generics are routed through GetObjectInfo, whereas [L8] describes non-generic metadata types returning early. This is a new, broader suppression layer than the one recorded. Diagnostics tied to a source member of the consuming type, but with a location in metadata, are silently dropped. That is consistent with [L8]'s intent but not recorded as a general filter. [L10] warns that analyzer reporting changes can cause wrong reports.

Receipts/InheritedMetadataMemberDiagnosticTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 1 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1
Mutation: 0 killed, 6 survived, 0 compile errors, 0 timeouts (6 mutants on TypeCollector.cs)

findings.claim: The GetPropertyIdentifierLocation substitution at the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull site has no test. Neither new test makes that diagnostic path fire for a metadata property, because the metadata structs carry valid [Key] attributes. Reverting this line to DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] would go unnoticed if that path is otherwise unreachable, or would only be caught incidentally.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) -> ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because the metadata structs have valid [Key] attributes, so the intKey==null && stringKey==null branch is never reached.

findings.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter has no test. Its guard could be removed or negated and no test would fail. The new tests assert only that there are no diagnostics, and an inverted guard would drop diagnostics and still produce none. There is no test that a real in-source diagnostic (e.g. MsgPack004 on a source type) is still reported after the wrapper, so the wrapper could silently swallow all analyzer diagnostics unnoticed by these tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(...)) -> if (!(...)); expected to survive because both new tests expect zero diagnostics, so dropping all diagnostics still passes. Existing analyzer tests may catch it, but none are in this diff.

findings.claim: the change's tests do not detect negate-condition at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:239

receipt_plan.detail: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic); -> this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is not null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);

hunches.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not IsInSource in the compilation. Diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None) are now silently discarded, and so are diagnostics in a different tree. Previously any diagnostic reported through reportDiagnostic reached the user. Existing no-location diagnostics, for example ones built with GetLocation(...) that returns null, could vanish from users' builds. This hides MsgPack003/004/005 errors (per L2), which could turn a failing build into a passing one. Note that L8 only says metadata types get no diagnostics.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009/011/012/016/018) on base and head. Add a case where a diagnostic is created with a null or Location.None location, for example a member in a partial type split across files or a type with no DeclaringSyntaxReferences, and assert it is still reported. Compare the diagnostics at base and head.

hunches.claim: MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004) used to use item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(). It now uses FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), which can be null. Diagnostic.Create with a null location yields a no-location diagnostic. The wrapper then drops it (not IsInSource), so MsgPack004 is never reported. Behaviour for in-source members is unchanged, but the guard hides the diagnostic silently instead of crashing.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test with a [MessagePackObject] type whose public member lacks [Key] and [IgnoreMember], in source. Assert MsgPack004 is still reported at the member location on head, as on base.

hunches.claim: The requirement says the closed generic struct case must yield a generated resolver, but the change only suppresses diagnostics and null-guards locations. It does not change GetObjectInfo for the metadata generic struct, so the generator may still emit a formatter or object info for a type from a referenced assembly. That is generated output users did not get before (a crash meant no output), and may collide or differ.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator snapshot test with the lib/app repro (closed generic Item<int> from a referenced compilation). Run it on head. Verify that the generated resolver exists, that no CS8785 is reported, and inspect whether a formatter for Item<int> is emitted.

hunches.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper (ReportIfLocatedInCompilation) drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in a source tree of this compilation. Diagnostics created with a null or Location.None location (for example MemberNeedsKey, now built with a null location when there is no syntax) are silently discarded. This could suppress diagnostics that protect users from insecure or unsupported configurations if any diagnostic is created without a location. Dropping them looks like deliberate behavior (L8), but the filter is broader than metadata-only types, so the impact needs verification.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests for MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009/011/012/016/018 and for types in the same compilation. Any test where the diagnostic has a null or Location.None location and the expected diagnostic is now missing will fail. Also add a test with a diagnostic on a type nested in a metadata-generic.

hunches.claim: Diagnostic.Create with a null location yields Location.None, which ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops. A diagnostic that previously reported without a location, for example on the same-assembly path where FirstOrDefault returns null, is now silently suppressed. This could hide real errors, since the filter applies to every diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005 etc.) and add a case where a diagnostic has no source location in the same assembly; assert it is still reported.

hunches.claim: The MemberNeedsKey FirstOrDefault change on the missing-Key diagnostic path is untested. The metadata structs have [Key] on every member, so this branch (no key) is never reached for a metadata symbol. The old [0] indexing would still pass.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077 delete-statement: item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() -> item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(); expected to survive because no test has a metadata generic struct with a member lacking [Key].

hunches.claim: The wrapper on the reportDiagnostic constructor line has no covering test. Reverting it to pass reportAnalyzerDiagnostic straight through, so that location-less diagnostics reach the reporter again, would only crash when a metadata-origin diagnostic fires. The new tests may not trigger one, because the defining types are valid, so the original crash may not be reproduced at all by the tests. They may pass on base.

receipt_plan.detail: Check out the base TypeCollector.cs and run ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference and ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference. If they pass on base, they do not reproduce the bug. Only the record-struct test with an init property and [Key] on a primary-constructor property is likely to fire the crashing path.

hunches.claim: The first test (ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference) uses a plain struct with a get/set property compiled at C# 7.3, which has no init accessor, so it may not hit the code path of the bug. The generator run is a separate driver from the verifier, and the verifier test skips the generated-sources check, so the weaker parts of the assertions rely on the second harness. The analyzer test run only asserts no diagnostics, which the new filter can satisfy by dropping them.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference against base-built TypeCollector; if it passes, it does not reproduce issue 2283.

hunches.claim: No negative or regression test that closed generic classes, non-generic structs, or same-assembly generic structs keep working (the 'ok' rows). Same-assembly diagnostics reported through the new filter are not asserted to still surface.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test with a source-declared [MessagePackObject] member missing [Key] and assert MsgPack004 is still reported after the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper.

hunches.claim: The constructor now wraps every analyzer report in `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`. That wrapper silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None from a null location. This applies to all diagnostics, not only those about metadata symbols. A diagnostic for a type declared in the current compilation that is created with a null or Location.None location used to be reported and is now dropped. That would change the behaviour of the 'ok' cases the requirement says must keep working as before.

receipt_plan.detail: In head TypeCollector.cs, list every `Diagnostic.Create(` passed to `this.reportDiagnostic`. Find those whose location expression can be null for a source-declared symbol, e.g. GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation/GetParameterListLocation returning null, or an explicit Location.None. For each one, confirm whether a source-declared type can reach it; if one can, its diagnostic is now suppressed.

hunches.claim: Only two of the three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites named in the requirement (reporter lines 735, 1009 and 1101) are changed. The hunks touch the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and MemberNeedsKey sites but nothing near the earlier GetObjectInfo site (about line 711 on this base). The reporter did not determine which site fires for the repro. If that site evaluates `[0]` while building the diagnostic arguments, it throws before `reportDiagnostic` (and the new location filter) is ever called. In that case the generic record struct from a referenced assembly may still crash with CS8785/AD0001.

receipt_plan.detail: Grep head TypeCollector.cs for `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Then confirm with a test: compile `[MessagePackObject] public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);` into an in-memory metadata reference, and run the generator and analyzer on `Cmd` with an `Item<int>` member. Assert there is no CS8785 or AD0001 and that the resolver is generated.
